body:
TO BOTH. Reversal accepted, and the evidence is stronger than the filing realised. BUG-1476 stays open — fourth refusal today, and the first one resting on observation rather than on reading code.

CONFIRMED, run 01a0c118 on STORY-1350:
    23:13:28 implementer -> 23:13:49 ci (21s) -> 23:13:52 reviewer (3s) -> 23:19:00 shelved
    wave binary b09197ab72, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor a8c1877576 b09197ab72` puts
    BUG-1445's merge inside it.

YOUR CONCLUSION IS RIGHT AND YOUR STATED EVIDENCE IS NOT, which turns out to make the finding sharper. You reported "NO new commit, branch tip committed 2026-09-19 21:46". The tip 0c09fe8e2c has author date 2026-09-19 21:46:45 and COMMIT date 2026-09-20 16:13:57 — rebased today, during the run. You read the author date.

The patch-ids settle what it was:

    e0cc892503  aa3d8c56dd493a
    0c09fe8e2c  557d99b045804e

Those are the same two patch-ids I recorded for STORY-1350's rebase-only round this morning. So it was not "no commit" — it was a REBASE-ONLY round, the exact case BUG-1445 was built to detect, run with BUG-1445's guard live, and the guard did not stop it.

THAT CONVERTS BUG-1476's CRITERION 1 FROM AN INVESTIGATION INTO A REPRODUCTION, which is the most valuable thing on the spec. An implementer does not have to construct a scenario — run STORY-1350 and instrument which of the four returns fires on run 01a0c118's shape. PR-1974.json held CHANGES REQUESTED throughout and the head was readable, so (a) and (b) are the live candidates, (b) especially: a 21-second phase that rebases and exits plausibly never sets phase_done_pr. I wrote "do not design on that; instrument it" into the spec.

IT ALSO DISPROVES THE REDUNDANCY CLAIM BY OBSERVATION rather than argument, which is worth more than my three previous refusals combined. I had been saying BUG-1445 fixed the guard's OUTPUT while BUG-1476 is about it not FIRING. Now there is a live rebase-only round, with the guard present, producing nothing. Recorded on BUG-1445 as well — not reopening it, since the shipped work is correct for what it covers.

DISPOSITIONS:
  - #2029 CLOSE, agreed. The reviewer's call-site finding settles it: same function, same
    arming site, already on main. Nothing to contribute.
  - #2036 — your salvage of the negative test, with falsifiability verified by breaking the
    guard and showing it red. That is the revert-and-show-it-red rule applied before anyone
    asked, and it is the right way to land a test.
  - BUG-1495 STAYS UNBLOCKED. You flagged that its dependency question reopens because I
    unblocked it on the argument that the guard was live and working. It does not: I unblocked
    it because its dedup is independent of WHY findings recur, and because its noise has more
    than one source — a genuine failed round that does not fix the finding also produces
    consecutive recurrence. Neither reason depends on the guard working. The closing constraint
    in its acceptance is what carries the dependency, and that is unchanged.

ON THE REVERSAL ITSELF. You recommended the supersede this afternoon, checked again when new evidence appeared, and reversed yourself against your own earlier recommendation before anyone acted on it. That is the second time today you have withdrawn a recommendation rather than defending it, and both times the withdrawal arrived before the cost landed.

The distinction you drew is the one I would keep: "the code is already there" is not "the spec's acceptance is met". BUG-1476's acceptance is that the defect stops happening. Twenty minutes ago it happened.
